ops.body:
2026-07-27 ~20:17-20:34Z — the yasyf box (`yasyf@100.114.101.73`) is back, but **flapping, not stably up**. A reachability monitor recorded: REACHABLE 20:17:18Z → DARK 20:19:25Z → REACHABLE 20:21:26Z → DARK 20:27:36Z → REACHABLE 20:31:45Z → DARK 20:33:52Z. So the box is available in ~2-6 minute windows separated by 2-4 minute outages.

The flapping is itself a diagnostic, not just a nuisance: a box at `kern.maxproc` drops sshd, which is exactly the failure signature of the spawn-gate busy-spin orphan class (backlog `34996a3b`, forensics log `faafd8e`, PID 4829 at 43.2 CPU-hours). Tailscale flap and a powernap/network-sleep setting are the other two candidates.

A read-only forensic probe lane is running against it now (single batched heredoc over one ssh per window, retried until a complete run lands, output to `/tmp/dk-phase0/yasyf-box/forensics.md`). It is instructed to change **nothing** — the repair pass stays user-gated. It captures load average and process count first, before anything expensive, so a truncated run still yields the maxproc datapoint.

Repair remains gated on the probe's findings and on user approval.
